text.p: Severe flooding is ongoing in the US North Plains across many river systems. The next few days should feature cooler than normal temperatures and no widespread heavy, precipitation. Cool temperatures keep snowmelt slow, preventing even worse flooding.

Typhoon Isa, with 85 mph winds, is near 10n/148e, moving west at 12 mph. This is about 315 miles southeast of Guam in the southwest Pacific. Isa will become a major risk to shipping during the next 24-48 hours as the system strengthens rapidly. It is expected to have winds of more than 130 mph in about 48 hours. It is also a strong risk to the Northern Mariana islands during this period. Guam and vicinity will likely see very heavy rains and very strong winds during the period. Damage due to winds and flooding is expected.
There are no further emergency statements at this time.
